maker_not_judge: the ask was shaped by rm-detached-bench-flyer-tier-three-rebuild-easy-wings-only-1795708955; this run made no Murrelith art or def
subject: RM_Murrelith
question: (a) one shared cut-out flip-book from the base static, so every coat flies as the base coat, or (b) a Harmony swap to a per-coat flip-book. Is a coat that changes look on take-off a flaw a player would reject?
answer: Yes, a coat that changes look on take-off is a flaw that the player sees. Pick (b).
evidence: Engine (measured, decompile rw16): AnimationDefGenerator_Flying builds fly animations per PawnKindDef lifeStage from flyingAnimationFramePathPrefix; Pawn_FlightTracker.GetBestFlyAnimation reads only pawn.kindDef.lifeStages; AlternateGraphic has no flying field. So under (a), every coat flies as one look.

Exposure (measured, def): alternateGraphicChance 0.857 over 6 coats, wildGroupSize 2~5, MaxFlightTime 10 / FlightCooldown 5. About 6 of 7 murreliths would change look at every take-off and change back at every landing, and a flock shows the mismatch side by side.

The coats differ in shape and colour, not only shade (looked: sheet D:\ClaudeWork\scratch\murrelith_judge\coats.png). Base: compact crested body, gold-cream ribbons. V_C..V_F: slender heron-like body, wings spread, iridescent ribbons with drip tips. V_G: long-legged standing heron. V_H: same body with grey-silver ribbons. Under (a), V_H's silver ribbons turn iridescent gold in the air, and the slim heron coats turn into the stocky crested base. A player reads that as a different animal, not as the same bird in flight.

Vanilla precedent (measured, Data/*/Defs): no vanilla flyer pairs flight with alternateGraphics; where a flyer's ground look differs (Duck, Quail, Peacock by sex) vanilla ships a second flip-book (flyingAnimationFramePathPrefixFemale), and Chicken/Locust use flyingAnimationInheritColors so a tint carries into flight. Vanilla never lets a bird's flight look contradict its ground look.

Owner: he kept these coats ('B, C, D, E, F, G, H are all beautiful', 2026-10-16, item FLYER_VARIANTS_INSTALL_MORE_FACES_PLEASE). Option (a) hides each kept coat whenever the bird flies; E3 (a delegated call never displaces a picture that he KEPT) argues against a choice that swaps his kept coats out in flight.

Attainable (measured, decompile): Verse.PawnGraphicUtils.GetGraphicIndex(pawn) is public and deterministic (thingIDNumber seed); GetBestFlyAnimation is a public static, so one Harmony postfix that returns the coat's own AnimationDef (built like AnimationDefGenerator_Flying.CreateAnimFromFrames) is small.
build_notes: Coats whose looks are the same body and palette may share one flip-book set; the bar is that no coat changes look at take-off, not a count of sets (a count of art variants is no bar).

V_C..V_F statics already draw the wings spread. The cut-out recipe (flyer_stable_body_study.md 3.1) locks the body by construction; the builder picks the static that gives a clean body per look. This is a note, not a constraint.
Never live-test the flight and never capture images of flight. Verify the swap by a deterministic read: two pawns of different coat index get different fly AnimationDefs.
The build waits for the FeverWood owner hold (src/RimMandrake/rimflow/mod_owner_hold.json).

verdicts.quote: A delegated call (a call that an agent makes in the owner's place) never displaces a picture that he KEPT. / Matches its sibling keeps: the other sex, lifestages and variants that he already approved set the style, palette and scale.
verdicts.seen: under (a) a V_H murrelith (grey-silver ribbons, slim heron body) takes off as the gold-ribboned stocky crested base bird; 6 of 7 birds swap look each flight
verdicts.redo_brief: give each coat (or each group of identical-looking coats) its own cut-out flip-book and pick it at flight by the pawn's alternate graphic index

verdicts.picture: option (b): per-coat flip-books with a Harmony swap
verdicts.notes: keeps each kept coat's look through take-off and landing; matches vanilla's practice of a second flip-book wherever a ground look differs

evidence: option (b) is a whole-body directional flip-book per coat

refusals.observed: option (a) shows the base coat in flight for every coat, so each of his kept coats V_C..V_H is replaced in the air by a different-looking bird
refusals.would_pass: each coat's flight look matches its ground coat in body shape and ribbon colour

smallest_fix.what: cut-out flip-books per distinct look, plus one Harmony postfix on Pawn_FlightTracker.GetBestFlyAnimation that picks by pawn.GetGraphicIndex()

refusals.criterion_why: he kept the coats by name; a flight look that hides them displaces them where the player sees it

proposals: A line for the brief: a flyer's flight look matches its ground look (coat and sex), as vanilla does; evidence: this ask, and vanilla Duck/Quail/Peacock female flip-books.
